concentration_time_figure.note: True plasma concentration versus time curves after single i.v. (Fig. 3A, Fig. 3C) and single s.c. (Fig. 3B) dosing in Balb/c mice; Fig. 3A fitted to a two-compartment model, Fig. 3B to a non-compartmental model.

bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence quantification of Alexa488-labelled polypeptide in whole blood against an Alexa488 standard curve; 125I gamma counting (automated gamma counter) for the biodistribution arm
bioanalytical_quote: The concentration of fluorescently labeled polymer in the blood was calculated using a standard curve of Alexa 488 (Figure S3 and S4).
notes: Half-lives in Tables 2 and 3 are explicitly elimination half-lives (t1/2β): METHODS states 'The elimination half-life (t1/2β) was calculated from the slope of the linear regression fit to the elimination portion of the log concentration vs. time curve', and the RESULTS text names them 'elimination half-life'. The column header is t1/2 (h) - a time, not a rate constant - so no ln2/k conversion was needed or performed. No absorption half-life is reported anywhere in the body; tmax (s.c. only, Table 3) is the only absorption-related parameter and was NOT used to derive an absorption half-life. Cmax is defined in METHODS ('tmax for s.c. PK data was determined as the time required to reach Cmax') but no numeric Cmax value is printed in the body. AUC for the (VPKEG)80/(VPGAG)80 length series is deferred to Table S1 (supplementary) and so is recorded as not reported in body. PEG-48kDa (14 h) and XTEN432 (9 h) half-lives quoted in the Discussion are cited literature values for substances NOT administered in this study, so they are not listed as agents. GLP1 fusion arms have efficacy (blood glucose, body weight) but no drug-concentration PK. Mouse and human serum albumin were binding partners in a native-PAGE assay rather than administered agents, so they are not listed as agents; because purified albumin protein was used rather than serum, that assay is classified in vitro and no ex vivo work is present.
